subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept these 14 executable action updates as one rebased batch after targeted exact-head proof, or split the privilege-sensitive action families for separate review?
rationale: The patch changes code executed with repository tokens, publishing credentials, security-scanning permissions, and OpenAI keys, while the protected `security` label requires explicit maintainer handling.

options.title: Accept after targeted proof
options.body: Rebase onto current `main` and merge the batch only after the affected security, token, release, and Codex workflows pass on that exact head.

options.title: Split sensitive families
options.body: Separate token, CodeQL, Docker publishing, and Codex action upgrades so each trust boundary can be validated and rolled back independently.

options.title: Defer the batch
options.body: Leave the current pins in place until upstream changes or repository CI provide clearer runtime evidence.

recommendation.title: Accept after targeted proof
recommendation.body: Rebase onto current `main` and merge the batch only after the affected security, token, release, and Codex workflows pass on that exact head.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the documented project maintainer and has recent ownership evidence in release and workflow hardening.
